subject.title: /new and /reset should support @agent targeting in multi-agent channels

question: What should `/new` and `/reset` do when more than one agent is eligible in a channel and the user does not specify a target?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the safe default, target syntax, and authorization model affect session ownership across Discord, Telegram, Slack, text commands, and native slash commands.

options.title: Require explicit target in ambiguous rooms
options.body: Require an explicit agent/account target when multiple agents are eligible, and return a chooser or refusal when no target is provided.

options.title: Choose active agent by heuristic
options.body: Pick the active or highest-context agent for no-target commands, improving convenience but risking surprising destructive resets.

options.title: Reset active participants together
options.body: Reset all agents participating in the current thread, preserving group-room semantics but making broad reset behavior intentional.

recommendation.title: Require explicit target in ambiguous rooms
recommendation.body: Require an explicit agent/account target when multiple agents are eligible, and return a chooser or refusal when no target is provided.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the shared native command target resolver and earlier native target-session behavior that this contract would extend.
